answer: A sybil defense is to judge identities by a long, checkable trail of work, not by how many appear at once. A nebula looks vast, but it is mostly gas: new accounts can be spun up cheaply, and their sheer number proves nothing. A sparrow is small yet real, returning day after day with delivered tasks and peer attestations. An agent economy can treat a meadow the same way: count only plants that keep growing, not seeds scattered overnight. New identities should start with small supervised jobs and almost no weight, gaining influence only as their record lengthens, so creation cannot buy standing
